images.title: No shared prime factor
images.purpose: Show that 80 and 63 have no prime factor in common, so they are co-prime.
images.composition: Two rows of dots, one above the other, with generous space, and one short line of text below.
images.exact_structure: Top row: 5 teal #0072B2 dots evenly spaced with the label 80 = 2×2×2×2×5 above it. Second row: 3 amber #E69F00 dots evenly spaced with the label 63 = 3×3×7 above it. No dot is joined to any other. Below, centred: one reddish purple #CC79A7 text line. Exactly 8 dots, 3 labels.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any line joining a teal dot to an amber dot
images.takeaway: No common prime factor means the numbers are co-prime.
images.description: A row of five teal dots for 80 and a row of three amber dots for 63, with no shared factor between them.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to look for any prime that appears in both rows and say what that means.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a clean contrast of two separate factor rows; one image is enough.
